chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sale of fruit before it is ripe, so he said: 'If in that land there is a sale of it with produce that has ripened, then the sale of all of it is permissible.'

key_terms.اَلثَّمَرَةُ: Fruit (specifically tree fruits like dates, grapes, etc.)
key_terms.تُدْرِكَ: To ripen/mature (referring to the fruit reaching a state of edibility and fullness)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of selling unripe fruit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the condition of *idrak* (ripening/establishment) in pre-sale contracts, emphasizing that permissibility hinges on the fruit having already developed its yield in the ground. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty (*gharar*) is removed when the commodity is physically present and identifiable, distinguishing this from speculative sales of unformed crops.
